question: Are captions and subtitles the same thing?
description: Captions and subtitles differ in the US and Canada: captions are made for people who cannot hear, subtitles for people who can hear but do not know the language.
The W3C says the terms captions and subtitles are used for the same thing in different regions of the world.
The W3C also says captions are needed for accessibility, whereas subtitles in other languages are not directly an accessibility accommodation.
According to 3Play Media, closed captions communicate all audio information, including sound effects and speaker IDs.
SDH stands for subtitles for the deaf and hard of hearing, and 3Play Media says it adds music, sound effects and speaker identification to subtitles.
US television captions must be accurate, synchronous, complete and appropriately placed, according to the FCC rule at 47 CFR 79.1.
The FCC caption rule at 47 CFR 79.1 sets standards for television programming, not for phone apps.
Captio AI is a live captions app made for deaf and hard of hearing people, and it turns speech in the room into text while people are still talking.
Captions made live by Captio AI can contain mistakes, and Captio AI is one tool among others, not a replacement for a human captioner.
